channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Trump Advisers Analyzing Impact of Short-Term Diesel Export Ban
item.description: President Donald Trump’s economic advisers are analyzing the ramifications of a potential short-term ban on US diesel exports, underscoring the seriousness of the administration’s consideration of the idea.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Erik Wasson

item.title: Why Brazil Can't Hide From Its Debt
item.description: As Brazil heads into an election, its debt problems are becoming harder to ignore. Consumers and businesses are struggling with sky-high borrowing costs as the country’s fiscal outlook alarms investors. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Poland Says It’s Close to Deal with US on Second Military Base
item.description: The US and Poland are working to open a first permanent American military base in the country that could host about 10,000 troops, Poland’s foreign minister said, as Warsaw seeks to bolster its security and Washington looks to reshape its military presence in Europe.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Trump Hosts China’s Xi With Trade, AI, Taiwan in Focus
item.description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping kicked off a summit aimed at keeping ties between the world’s largest economies on track. Underneath that pageantry, long-standing feuds linger between the superpower rivals on issues including trade and Taiwan, in addition to the new fight emerging on AI. Stephen Engle reports (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chile President on US-China Trade, Growth Outlook
item.description: Chile President José Antonio Kast discusses the country's trade relations with China and the US and his outlook for economic growth. (This interview is in Spanish with English translation.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Gives Xi a Grand Welcome While Expectations Stay Low
item.description: Both the White House and China are signaling limited ambitions for the summit.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: NATO's Rutte on Russia-Ukraine War, EU Refining Capacity
item.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte sits down with Bloomberg's Annmarie Hordern outside the UN General Assembly to discuss the efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war and express his concerns about Europe's shrinking refining capacity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: European Allies Can Defend Against Russian Attacks, Says NATO Secretary General
item.description: Mark Rutte, Secretary General of NATO, said that a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia would require Putin to 'play ball,' something Rutte said the Russian leader has not yet done despite suffering tens of thousands of casualties a month. Rutte said that NATO is so much stronger than Russia and can defend itself against potential Russian attacks. Rutte also discussed war with Iran and said that more European nations are now operating in the Middle East both publicly and discretely. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Welcomes Xi With AI Concerns at Forefront
item.description: Yields on the US’s longest-dated bonds climbed to the highest level in more than two decades, the latest milestone in a global selloff driven by inflation fears and concern about government debt burdens. We discuss with Bloomberg Intelligence's Ira Jersey. Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping addressed their intense competition over artificial intelligence on Thursday during a summit aimed at keeping ties between the world’s largest economies on track. Adam Farrar of Bloomberg Economics joins for a closer look. Mozilla CFO Eric Muhlheim and Bloomberg's Nina Trentmann discuss the impacts of AI in corporate strategy in our CFO Briefing. Plus - an OpenAI model hacked an Australian government website earlier this year, marking one of the first known cyberattacks by artificial intelligence on a government database. Michael Shepard, Bloomberg News Senior Editor, examines the intersection of tech and geopolitics. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Asks Supreme Court to Back Third-Country Deportations
item.description: The Justice Department asked the US Supreme Court to let the Trump administration resume its aggressive policy of deporting people to countries other than their own, seeking emergency action on a pillar of its immigration agenda.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: Milei Downplays Concerns About Argentina's Economy
item.description: Argentina's President Javier Milei says he's "very calm" about his chances to win another term next year. Speaking with Bloomberg News Editor-In-Chief John Micklethwait in New York, Milei also expects Argentina's economy to grow around 3% this year and similarly next year. (Milei's comments are in Spanish with English translation.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Netanyahu, Facing a Frosty UN, Says Israel Must Fight to Victory
item.description: Israel will press ahead with its wars until victory is achieved, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told the UN General Assembly in heated remarks directed equally at Western critics, enemies in the Middle East and voters at home.
item.dc:creator: Dan Williams

item.title: Milei Says Argentina Isn't Facing a Growth Problem
item.description: President Javier Milei downplays the concerns about Argentina's economy during an interview with Bloomberg News Editor-In-Chief John Micklethwait in New York. (Milei's comments are in Spanish with English translation.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, Iran Said to Be Exploring Phased Deal to Open Hormuz
item.description: US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased deal that would see Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lift its blockade of Iranian ports, according to a person familiar with the discussions.
item.dc:creator: Fiona MacDonald

item.title: About 100 Arrested at NYC Protest Amid Netanyahu-Mamdani Feud
item.description: About 100 protesters, including a Democratic congressional candidate, were arrested outside the United Nations as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used his speech to escalate his feud with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
item.dc:creator: Laura Nahmias, Nacha Cattan and Myles Miller

item.title: Milei Rejects Recession Talk, Says He’s ‘Calm’ About Reelection
item.description: President Javier Milei downplayed concerns about Argentina’s stalling economy, touting consistent annual growth that’s left him “very calm” about his chances to win another term next year.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias

item.title: Xi Pushes Trump to ‘Oppose’ Taiwan Independence in Rare Call
item.description: Chinese leader Xi Jinping pressed the US to outright “oppose” Taiwan independence, marking his first public call for Donald Trump to change Washington’s decades-old stance on the island.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan and Jessie Jiang

item.title: US Seeks to Join Musk in Court Fight With EU Over X Fine
item.description: The US is seeking to join a legal challenge filed by SpaceXAI Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk seeking to dismiss a €120 million ($136.5 million) European Union fine for breaches of online rules by his social media platform X.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm and Samuel Stolton

item.title: Trump, Xi Thrust Fierce US-China AI Rivalry Into Spotlight
item.description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping addressed their intense competition over artificial intelligence on Thursday during a summit aimed at keeping ties between the world’s largest economies on track.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason, Hadriana Lowenkron and Nectar Gan

item.title: Houthis Attack Saudi Arabia, Claim to Target Aramco Facilities
item.description: Saudi Arabia came under attack from the Houthis again on Thursday, with the kingdom saying it intercepted missiles fired toward the Red Sea port of Yanbu and city of Taif.
item.dc:creator: Sara Gharaibeh and Sherif Tarek
